body:
- The professional cycle playbook is: (1) identify where the sector sits in its earnings and multiple cycle (trough multiple on trough earnings = maximum asymmetry), (2) track leading indicators such as order inflows, the government capex budget, capacity utilization (RBI OBICUS), credit growth and commodity prices, and (3) recognize that late-cycle re-rating driven by reflexive flows ends abruptly.
- The 2007 to 2021 capital goods hangover is the base-rate warning: buying a cyclical at peak can mean a decade or more of dead money.

body:
- Retail workflow: monthly, scan MF portfolio changes (new entries and increases across multiple AMCs), quarterly shareholding patterns (promoter pledge, FII/DII trend), and daily bulk/block deals. Use these as idea and confirmation signals, never as theses.
- Apply a Marcellus-style forensic screen first, before getting excited about growth: CFO/EBITDA, contingent liabilities, related-party transactions, auditor changes, capitalised costs, and the yield on cash.
- SPIVA shows that even well-resourced professionals mostly fail to beat the index after fees. A retail stock picker should run a low-cost index core and keep active bets as a satellite.

`theme:sector-nbfc-hfc` · confidence: single-source · tickers: BAJFINANCE, CHOLAFIN, SHRIRAMFIN, MUTHOOTFIN, BAJAJHFL, AAVAS, CREDITACC

**How it makes money:** Wholesale-funded specialist lending; RoA = spread - opex - credit cost; RoE via 4–7x leverage.

**Metrics that matter:**
- AUM growth (disbursement mix)
- NIM / spread
- cost of borrowing & ALM buckets
- credit cost
- GS3/NS3 + Stage-2
- opex/AUM
- RoA/RoE
- CRAR & borrowing mix (bank vs bond vs CP)

**Value chain and where margins sit:** Funding (banks, bond markets, securitisation) -> origination (branches, DSAs, digital partners) -> collections. Margins are highest in unsecured and MFI (with high credit cost), steady in gold, vehicles and affordable housing, and thinnest in prime home loans, where banks compete.

**Cycle drivers:** Liquidity and spreads, repo cycle (NBFCs benefit with a lag as liabilities reprice), RBI regulation (scale-based regulation, risk weights, gold LTV), rural income for MFI and vehicle books.

**Lead indicators (public India data):**
- RBI sectoral deployment: bank credit to NBFCs
- RBI NBFC credit release (monthly)
- MFIN Micrometer (quarterly)
- CRIF High Mark / CIBIL delinquency
- CP/NCD spreads over G-sec
- Monthly disbursement updates (Bajaj Fin quarterly AUM update)

**What separated winners from losers:** Winners: granular retail books, cross-cycle credit cost discipline, a diversified liability franchise, group or parent backing. Losers: ALM mismatch (short CP funding long loans), related-party or real-estate developer exposure, single-product concentration (MFI), aggressive gross-to-net provisioning games.

**Valuation ranges and peaks/troughs:** P/B vs RoE x growth. Bajaj Finance peak ~10x P/B (2021), compressed to ~5x. Vehicle/gold NBFC 1.5–3.5x; affordable HFCs 2–4x at peak (2021–24). Crisis troughs: post-IL&FS 2018–19 and Mar 2020 (many <1x).

**Current state (Nov 2026):** NBFC credit +15.4% YoY Sep 2026 vs 13.3% a year ago (RBI); housing, gold and vehicle loans accelerating. Bajaj Finance AUM ₹5,84,750 cr (+26.5%) at 30 Sep 2026. ICRA moved NBFC-MFI outlook to Stable (FY27 AUM growth 20–25%). HFCs recovered from FY26 stress, with 4QFY26 disbursements up 19.5% across 10 listed HFCs.

**Classic traps:**
- Growth with falling yield = taking more risk for less
- Low credit cost early in a seasoning book
- Write-offs that keep GNPA flat (look at gross credit cost)
- Off-balance-sheet co-lending/DLG
- Treating a promoter group's halo as capital

body:
- SSSG: FY25 12.3%, FY26 **11.0%** `[AR26]`. Q2 FY27 5.4% (about 9% adjusted for an 18-day festive shift), H1 FY27 7.7% `[PPT-Q2]`.
- **What drives it** `[CC-Q3FY26]`: about 70% from transactions (number of bills) and 30% from bill value. Bills grew about 10% YoY like-for-like `[ELARA]`. Average bill was ₹875 (FY25). Loyalty members: 18.1 cr registered, and **95% of revenue comes from loyalty customers** `[PPT-Q2]`. That gives VMM a large first-party data asset, and it means the "registered" count is cumulative and inflated (anyone who gives a phone number at checkout is counted).
- **SSSG definition:** stores operational for at least 15 months at the start of the quarter, *excluding* stores closed for "refurbishment, area reduction, or any one-off reason" `[PPT-Q2]`. Ask: how many stores are excluded each quarter? Excluded stores can quietly hold the weak ones.
- **Cannibalisation:** UP/Haryana are being deepened with small-format stores. Management claims the same revenue per sq ft `[HSIE]`. That is not yet testable from disclosures, because SFS are not split out (only 18 stores). The test is North-region revenue per store, which HSIE notes is still the highest. "West is the only region to contract in FY26" `[HSIE]`.

body:
| Question | Evidence | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| Is the "cheap" multiple on peak earnings? | TTM EPS ₹137.6 = record (FY19 peak ₹80, FY24 ₹110); OPM 12.5% in Q2 = record (prior peak 11.8%); FY26 M&HCV ~480k = FY19 peak 476k; FY27 guided 500k+; capacity ~98% used; steel and gear supply constrained | **Yes.** On 10-year normalised EPS the P/E is 25.8x. The last time the stock looked "cheap" at a peak (16x at FY19) it fell 80% in 18 months |
| Is a cycle turn dated? | Management: pre-buys "until April of next year" ahead of regulation changes; "beyond April up to September is a watch" `[T-Q2FY27]` | **A known, dated catalyst** inside our call window (Apr–Sep 2027) |
| Is the business deteriorating under the cycle? | Like-for-like FY26 revenue ~flat vs industry +16% (gross-up) `[EST]`; content per vehicle +0.9%/yr since FY19; 66% one customer | **Possibly** (single-source industry data; open flag) |
| Capital allocation history | Debt-free; net cash built to ₹394 cr (15% of mcap); payout ~30%; no buyback; capex ~₹70 cr/yr + ₹120 cr phase 1 at the top of the cycle; Hosur closed; supplier loans ₹5.6 cr | **Conservative, not value-destroying**; cash drag (treasury ~7.5%) and capex timing pro-cyclical |
| Who takes value before minorities? | Technical fee 4.5% of sales, annually renewed; total parent take ~5.8% of sales / 54% of core EBITDA (fee + warranty + BFL services) | **The main governance question**; minorities pushed back once (Dec-2024) |
| Fraud / solvency trap? | Clean audit, AA-, no pledge, ICR 110x | **No** |
**Conclusion:** cheap because the market is correctly discounting a cyclical peak and a parent take; **not a fraud or solvency trap; partly a
cyclical value trap**. The deep dive's job here was to say *which kind of cheap* — it found the cycle and the fee, not a hidden mispricing.

*Method calibration, not stock picking. Research, not SEBI-registered advice.*
Started 2026-11-24. Builds **stage 2 (hard filters)** and feeds **stage 6** (the decision card's survival cap,
`tools/decision/decision_card.py` v1.2). The combined-avoid test (`combined_avoid_india.md`, L35,
decision:pead-avoid-plus-redflag-survival-cap) adopted a cap only when a bottom-two SUE result coincides with
pledge > 25% or interest cover < 1.5x. Its own post-hoc reading: group C (red flag, no miss) halves 15.1% of the
time, ≈ 2.5× clean firms, so the flag, not the miss, carries the tail risk. That broader rule was not
pre-registered. This file tests it.
**Unlocks:** if adopted, the card's cap becomes a standing stage-2 size rule (independent of the PEAD window), the
nightly solvency/pledge screen feeds it directly, and stage 4 deep dives start with the balance-sheet question for
every flagged firm. If not, the cap stays tied to the PEAD window and the flags stay "look harder".

body:
- **H12 (primary):** lowest weekly close in (entry, entry + 52 weeks] ≤ 0.5 × entry close. E: `halve12` as already
  computed. P: computed from the chart series with px_T (last close ≤ T) as the entry.
- **FAIL3:** E: lowest weekly close ≤ 0.2× entry within 156 weeks, or the firm's series stops within 156 weeks and
  the firm is on a distress list (`distress` = 1). P: `o_fail` (5-year: liquidation, compulsory delisting, or ≤ 0.2×),
  as published.
- **XS52, XS156:** price return to the last weekly close ≤ entry + h weeks + 3 days minus the mean return of
  size-matched controls (E: all event-universe firms with a close on the entry Friday, mcap ×0.5–×2, ≥ 5 firms,
  same exit rule — the survivorship check's control rule, extended to 52 / 156 weeks; P: other panel snapshots of the
  same T, mcap ×0.5–×2, ≥ 5, weighted mean).
- **WIN3 (winner):** E: price ratio at 156 weeks ≥ 3. P: `winner` (5-year R5 ≥ 3, published).
- **Winner cost** = share of WIN3 cases that were CARD-flagged at entry (event-level in E; also at firm level: share
  of firms with ≥ 1 WIN3 event whose WIN3 events were *all* flagged, i.e. firms the cap would have kept us out of
  entirely). P: weighted share of winners flagged. Reported next to the share of halvings/failures flagged.
